A: Indicates a letter of the series A through Z in aeronautical codes, used as a designator for airway segments, holding patterns, or approach procedure identification.
A/A: Indicates a letter of the series A through Z in aeronautical codes, used as a designator in air-to-air communications or reference coding.
AAL: Above aerodrome level. The vertical distance of an aircraft, obstacle, or terrain feature measured from the aerodrome elevation.
ABBREV: Abbreviation. A shortened form of a word or phrase used in aviation communications, NOTAM text, and aeronautical documentation to convey information concisely.
ABM: Abeam. A position relative to an aircraft or fix where the bearing to the reference point is 90 degrees to the right or left of the aircraft's track.
ABNDT: Abundant. A qualifier used in meteorological reports and NOTAM text to indicate a plentiful or copious amount of a weather phenomenon or condition.
ABV: Above. A spatial qualifier used in aviation communications and documentation indicating a position at a higher altitude or elevation than a referenced point.
ACC: Acceleration. The rate of change of velocity of an aircraft with respect to time, expressed in knots per second or G-force, relevant to aircraft performance and flight dynamics.
ACCEL: Accelerate. To increase the speed or velocity of an aircraft; used in performance calculations, takeoff procedures, and ATC instructions.
ACCUM: Accumulate or accumulation. A term used in aviation weather reports and NOTAM text indicating the build-up or collection of precipitation, ice, or other meteorological phenomena.
ACLS: Automatic carrier landing system. A ship-based precision approach and landing system that provides guidance and control for aircraft conducting carrier landings, typically using radar and data link.
ACNS: Aeronautical chart. A specialized map designed for air navigation, depicting airspace structure, navigation aids, terrain, obstacles, and other information essential for flight planning and execution.
ACP: Airport control panel. A control panel located in an air traffic control tower or airport operations center that allows remote control of airport lighting systems, including runway edge lights, approach lights, and visual aids.
ACPT: Accept. A phrase used in ATC communications to confirm receipt and compliance with a clearance, instruction, or request from air traffic control.
ACS: Airspace control system. A coordinated system of procedures, facilities, and personnel used to manage and control the use of airspace to ensure safe and efficient air traffic operations.
ACT: Active, activated, activity. A status indicator used in aviation to describe a facility, airspace, runway, or navigational aid that is currently in operational use or has been put into service.
ADDN: Addition or additional. A qualifier used in NOTAM text and aviation documentation to indicate supplementary information, extra items, or further details beyond the primary content.
ADJ: Adjacent. A spatial qualifier used in aviation documentation and communications to describe a location, airspace, or facility that is next to or adjoining a referenced point or area.
ADVS: Advisory service. A service provided by air traffic control or flight service stations that offers advice and information to pilots to assist in the safe conduct of flight, including weather and traffic advisories.
AFIS: Aerodrome flight information service. A service provided at an aerodrome that supplies information to aircraft to ensure safe and efficient aircraft movement, including weather, runway conditions, and traffic information.
AFM: Aircraft flight manual. A document approved by the aviation authority that contains the operating limitations, performance data, procedures, and systems information for a specific aircraft type.
AFS: Aeronautical fixed service. A telecommunications service between specified fixed points in the aeronautical network, used for the exchange of aeronautical messages, flight plans, and air traffic control data.
AFTN: Aeronautical fixed telecommunication network. A worldwide telecommunications network operated by ICAO for the exchange of aeronautical messages, flight plans, NOTAMs, and meteorological data between fixed aeronautical stations.
AGL: Above ground level. The vertical distance of an aircraft, obstacle, or terrain feature measured from the underlying ground surface directly beneath it.
AIC: Aeronautical information circular. A notice issued by an aeronautical information service containing information that does not qualify for a NOTAM or an amendment to an AIP, such as administrative or explanatory information.
AIM: Aeronautical information manual. A comprehensive publication containing information on air navigation procedures, airspace, airports, and other aeronautical data essential for flight operations.
AIRAC: Aeronautical information regulation and control. An ICAO system for the regular and coordinated distribution of aeronautical information updates at specified effective dates, ensuring all aviation stakeholders receive changes simultaneously.
AIRMET: Airman's meteorological information. An aviation weather advisory issued for weather conditions that may be hazardous to light aircraft, including moderate icing, moderate turbulence, sustained winds of 30 knots or more, and widespread visibility less than 3 statute miles.
AIS: Aeronautical information service. A service established by a state to collect, manage, and disseminate aeronautical information and data necessary for the safety, regularity, and efficiency of air navigation.
ALD: Available landing distance. The length of the runway that is declared available and suitable for the landing ground roll of an aircraft by the runway-owning authority.
ALS: Approach lighting system. A series of lights installed on the approach end of a runway that provides visual guidance to pilots during the final approach phase, indicating the runway alignment, roll guidance, and distance to the threshold.
ALT: Altitude. The vertical distance of an aircraft or object above mean sea level, expressed in feet or metres, used as a standard reference for air traffic control separation and flight planning.
ALTN: Alternate or alternating. A term used in aviation to describe an alternate aerodrome designated for diversion, or an alternating pattern of lights or signals used in navigational aids.
AMA: Area minimum altitude. The minimum altitude that may be used for flight operations within a defined area under instrument meteorological conditions, providing obstacle clearance and navigation signal reception.
AMC: Aeronautical meteorological centre. A centre designated to prepare and issue meteorological forecasts, warnings, and other meteorological information in support of air navigation within its area of responsibility.
AMDT: Amendment. A formal change or modification to an aeronautical document, such as an AIP, aeronautical chart, or instrument procedure, issued to correct or update information.
AMS: Aeronautical mobile service. A radiocommunication service between aircraft stations and aeronautical ground stations, or between aircraft stations, used for air traffic control and operational communications.
AMSL: Above mean sea level. The vertical distance of an object, terrain feature, or aircraft measured from the mean sea level datum, used as the standard reference for altitude and elevation measurements.
ANC: Airport noise control. Programs, procedures, and equipment implemented at an airport to monitor, mitigate, and manage aircraft noise impacts on surrounding communities.
ANS: Answer. A response from a called station in aeronautical communications, confirming receipt of a call or providing the information requested.
ANT: Antenna. A device used for transmitting and receiving radio frequency signals in aviation communication, navigation, and surveillance systems.
ANVDT: Adverse weather. Meteorological conditions that are unfavorable for flight operations, including low visibility, strong winds, thunderstorms, icing, and other hazardous weather phenomena.
AOC: Aerodrome obstruction chart. A chart depicting obstacles and obstructions in the vicinity of an aerodrome that may affect aircraft operations, used for obstacle clearance assessment and flight procedure design.
AOM: Aerodrome operating minima. The minimum weather conditions, including visibility and cloud ceiling, required for aircraft to take off, approach, and land at a specific aerodrome.
AP: Airport. A defined area on land or water intended for the arrival, departure, and ground movement of aircraft, including associated buildings, facilities, and equipment.
APC: Airport parking code. A code or identifier used to designate specific aircraft parking positions, stands, or gates at an airport for ground handling and ramp operations.
APCH: Approach. The phase of flight during which an aircraft descends from the en-route phase toward the destination airport for landing, following a specific instrument or visual procedure.
APDC: Aircraft parking and docking code. A standardized code used to designate aircraft parking positions and docking procedures at airport gates, ensuring safe and efficient ground handling.
APN: Apron. A defined area on an aerodrome intended for the parking, loading, unloading, refueling, and maintenance of aircraft, also known as a ramp.
APP: Approach control office. The air traffic control facility responsible for controlling IFR aircraft arriving at, departing from, and transiting the vicinity of an airport or group of airports within a terminal area.
APRX: Approximately. A qualifier used in aviation communications and documentation to indicate that a value, time, or quantity is estimated and may vary slightly from the stated figure.
ARP: Aerodrome reference point. The designated geographical location of an aerodrome, typically at or near the geometric center of the landing area, used for navigation and charting purposes.
ARST: Arresting. Relating to aircraft arresting systems, such as arresting cables, nets, or engineered materials used to decelerate aircraft during emergency landing situations or on short runways.
